comments.text: I’ve studied economic crashes for decades and what I’ve learned is the lessons learned by the crashes really are learned for the generations alive at the time but are forgotten 2-3 generations later.  We narrowly avoided financial crises in 1997 and again in 2001 only to NOT avoid 2008.  Unfortunately we’re setting up for almost the same setup as 1929, and while we have things like the FDIC and safety nets they lacked, the government is also in far worse shape thanks to decades of deficit spending.  Maybe we’ll finally learn the lessons for good this time. The smart approach isn’t always about knowing where the market goes next, it’s about knowing how to navigate the inevitable crash.
